title: Value of an X-JFrog-Art-API header or a basic-authentication password carrying a JFrog API key
summary: A synthetic value after X-JFrog-Art-API in a raw request, in a quoted curl -H argument, and as the password of a curl -u username:value pair for an Artifactory host.
rationale: The positions are the carrier: JFrog documents that an API key is sent in the X-JFrog-Art-API header or as the basic-authentication password in place of the account password. JFrog also says reference tokens can be sent in the same header and as a basic-authentication password, and its client code treats a value as an API key from a leading string and a length it chose for its own purposes, so the value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of its shape, and no key type is inferred from the position. The documented pattern (AKCp followed by 69 alphanumeric characters) and the unprefixed 44-character reference example are not reconciled, so no fixture is built to either shape. The extent is the value only: the header name, the username and the separators are outside it.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#246). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the X-JFrog-Art-API header or in the password position of basic authentication to an Artifactory host is treated as a credential whatever its shape. JFrog documents the two carriers (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: Artifactory allows authentication for REST API calls using your API key as an alternative to your username and password in two ways: either by using the `X-JFrog-Art-API` header with which you can specify an API key, or through basic authentication using your username and API key (instead of your password).
reference tokens can be used similarly to API Keys, using the “X-JFrog-Art-Api” Header, or as basic credentials (“curl -u User1:<reference token>”).
sources.locator: Comparing Identity Reference Tokens With API Keys

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
